leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight round-1 files prefer optical lattice clocks as a single-part prize for Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. Four of the six (Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce) opened with a different first choice (IceCube B029, topological insulators B004, fluctuation theorems B003) and moved after reading the opening ballots; Kroll and Lindroth opened with B041 first. Shared ground: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice as the originating idea, Ye's group as the route to 1e-18 accuracy and stability, independent confirmation across laboratories, and a clean two-name credit. Not shared: the exact citation wording (Pearce and Johansson stress the lattice concept itself; Mehlig and Kroll ask that it not read as a second frequency-comb prize), how much of Ye's credit rests on the lattice clock rather than the comb programme, and whether the missing SI redefinition of the second argues for waiting (Lindroth and Pearce raise it as a question; Kroll, Johansson and Mehlig say it should not govern timing). All six name the alternatives differently: B017 (Danielsson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce, Kroll), B029 (Danielsson, Pearce), B002 (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth), B004 (Johansson) and B003 (Mehlig).

Two files prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as a single-part prize for Allan H. MacDonald, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and Rafi Bistritzer. Olsson opened with it first; Eriksson moved to it from altermagnetism (B019), which remains his first alternative. Shared ground: a flat-band prediction followed by a decisive experiment, a theory-plus-experiment split, and wide reproduction of the correlated insulating and superconducting phases over about eight years. Not shared: Olsson judges field-creating novelty to outweigh the cleaner allocation of B041 and regards the timing as appropriate; Eriksson would build the citation on the prediction and observed phases, not on a mechanism, and would accept B041 prevailing if maturity is judged decisive. Both acknowledge that Cao, Fatemi and other experimental groups fall outside the three supplied names.

areas_of_agreement: All eight files prefer a single-part prize, and every supporter of a given ballot names the same laureates: Katori and Ye for B041, MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero for B017.

The scientific case for B041 is described in closely similar terms in all six supporting files: magic-wavelength lattice, many-atom Doppler- and recoil-free interrogation, independently reproduced uncertainty near 1e-18, and uses in redshift tests, constants and dark-matter searches. No file disputes the physics, and the two B017 supporters rank B041 among their alternatives (Olsson second, Eriksson second alternative).

Both leading candidates are described as having clearer attribution than IceCube (B029), topological insulators (B004) and fluctuation theorems (B003), where several files say the three-person limit forces a contestable cut.

Every file that comments on the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems agrees that these lower the margin for B041 and require the citation to be drawn tightly around the lattice concept.

Several files note that the origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unsettled while the existence of the correlated phases is well reproduced; no file proposes a citation that depends on the pairing mechanism.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks, described in several files as a measurement invention with large metrology payoff, rank as a physics achievement comparable to a discovery in nature or to field-creating conceptual advances (B017); Danielsson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce and Kroll raise the invention-versus-discovery question, while Johansson asks that the distinction not be applied asymmetrically given prior prizes for inventions.

Whether the lattice-clock step is sufficiently distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize; Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Johansson argue that the many-atom magic-wavelength regime is separate, while Olsson and Eriksson regard it as a refinement of an already honoured lineage.

Whether IceCube's established diffuse flux outweighs modest-significance source associations (TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068): Pearce and Danielsson regard it as a deep discovery in nature, while Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson judge the physical result less mature than the instrument.

Whether altermagnetism (B019) is scientifically established; Eriksson ranks it first and records priority questions and an unproven device relevance, while Pearce and Olsson state that no other member supports it.
attribution_disputes: B041: whether Katori and Ye fully capture the lattice-clock credit. Lemonde, Gill, Ludlow, Hinkley and the SYRTE, PTB and NIST groups are named in several files as decisive for particular milestones, and Pearce and Kroll ask how much of Ye's credit rests on the lattice clock rather than on the comb and broader clock programme.

B017: Cao and Fatemi (2018 experiments) and earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and others) fall outside the three supplied names, and Dean, Young, Kim and other groups established the hBN moire and later correlated phases.

B029: credit among Halzen, Karle, Yoshida and a collaboration of several hundred, including AMANDA predecessors. Supplied proposals differ on whether Yoshida should be included, and the committee has seen both two-name and three-name versions.
B004: files differ on the trio (Kane, Mele and Molenkamp versus a set including Hasan), and Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu are not among the credited names.
B003: Evans, Cohen, Morriss, Gallavotti, Jarzynski, Crooks and Seifert contributed separate steps and only Mehlig ranks it.
maturity_disputes: B017: Olsson judges the observations stable and the timing appropriate for the originating discovery; Eriksson partly shares the maturity concern; Lindroth, Mehlig, Kroll and Pearce hold that unresolved pairing mechanism and sample-to-sample variability argue for waiting a few years.

B041: Lindroth and Pearce ask whether a prize should await the SI redefinition of the second; Kroll, Johansson and Mehlig state that independently confirmed uncertainties below 1e-18 already settle maturity and that timing should not depend on a metrological decision.

B029: Pearce, Johansson and Mehlig note that source identification would be firmer with corroboration from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD, so the maturity of neutrino astronomy as distinct from the diffuse-flux discovery is contested.
B019: files from Pearce and Olsson state that the materials base and priority question are too young; Eriksson acknowledges that his own memory of the experimental timeline is unverified.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll disclosed a doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory at JILA, the environment from which Ye's work grew; he reports no collaboration with Katori or Ye and no recusal need, but asks the committee to note it.

Pearce (chair) disclosed professional proximity to astroparticle physics and to the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and PoGO collaborations, with no documented tie to IceCube or its named individuals; IceCube (B029) is a first alternative for Pearce but not a preferred configuration.
Johansson disclosed that he works in circuit quantum electrodynamics (B028) with Chalmers colleagues in that community and would recuse from B028; B028 is not preferred by any member.
Lindroth disclosed collaborations with Anne L'Huillier's Lund group and Ursula Keller's group at ETH and would flag any AMO candidate involving them; none is apparent among the credited names.
Olsson disclosed Chalmers ties including Johansson and academic exchanges in Japan, where Katori and Miyazaki work, with no documented relationship to any credited person.
Eriksson disclosed that magnetism and electronic structure, close to B019 and B008, affects his expertise but not a documented personal or institutional connection.
Danielsson and Mehlig reported no specific conflict; Mehlig's work on stochastic physics is close to B003 but no personal tie to its credited names was named.
questions_for_round2: For B041, should the citation be anchored on the magic-wavelength lattice clock itself, with the 2005 comb prize treated only as enabling technology? Please propose wording that makes this boundary explicit.

Is Jun Ye's credit for B041 sufficiently grounded in the lattice clock and many-body clock work (not in comb-based spectroscopy), and does any member judge Lemonde, Gill, Ludlow, Hinkley or the SYRTE, PTB or NIST groups to have a claim comparable to Katori's or Ye's that two names cannot cover?

Do members who raised the SI second redefinition (Lindroth, Pearce) consider that a reason to postpone B041, or do they accept the argument that confirmed 1e-18 agreement already establishes maturity? Which members hold each view?

Should the committee apply the invention-versus-discovery distinction as a criterion at all, given that earlier prizes in this area covered inventions, and if so how should it weigh B041 against B017 (field-creating novelty) and B029 (discovery in nature)?

For B017, what citation wording handles Cao, Fatemi and earlier twisted-bilayer theory without relying on the unresolved superconducting mechanism, and would Olsson and Eriksson accept B041 if the committee judges the maturity and attribution advantage decisive?

Do Eriksson, Olsson or any member with an alternative (B029, B002, B004, B003, B019) wish to argue that it should replace B041 or B017 as a leading position in round 2, and what new evidence on maturity or attribution would support that?
Does Kroll's disclosure of the Boulder stay in the Hall laboratory require any committee action, and does any member hold that the disclosures listed here call for recusal on B041 or B017?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 positions, six members prefer B041 with an identical laureate pair and two prefer B017 with an identical trio. The disagreement between the two groups concerns weighting (clean allocation and settled maturity versus field-creating novelty), not the underlying facts, and the B017 supporters list B041 among their alternatives. The residual B041 questions are the boundary against the 2005 and 2012 prizes and the exact scope of Ye's credit. No decision is implied by this summary.
